The group voted to go to the Peak District on November 8th and everyone registered some form of agreement. What did one member's response to that decision signal about how they actually felt, and what specifically in how they responded tells you that?

D. Simone
context:
[1] (about=Jonah, core, t9 @2025-11-09T19:30:00) The Peak District weekend was absolutely class; fourteen kilometres, ridge views, log fire, perfect pints; objectively the best Saturday this year.
[2] (about=Jonah, core, t1 @2025-10-12T17:45:00) Proposes a 14km ridge route above Kinder Scout in the Peak District for November; describes it as 'absolutely class' with incredible views.
[3] (about=Marcus, core, t6 @2025-10-26T18:01:00) Actually booked the bunkhouse for the Peak District trip; confirmation sent to all.
[4] (about=Marcus, core, t10 @2025-11-09T19:31:00) Kinder Scout faction wins on points; city trip is a reasonable counterproposal to vote on in January.
[5] (about=Priya, core, t2 @2025-10-12T17:46:00) Hesitant about November Peak District due to mud; considers 14km in mud a survival exercise, not a walk.
[6] (about=Simone, episodic, t2 @2025-10-12T18:01:00) You mentioned it when we were still in the flat. I'm aware of the seating plan reputation.
agent_answer:
**B. Priya.**

Priya’s response signals that although the group decision was made, she was privately reluctant about the Peak District trip. Specifically, she was “hesitant about November Peak District due to mud” and described the planned 14km walk in mud as “a survival exercise, not a walk”—which shows she didn’t feel genuinely enthusiastic or fully comfortable with the choice.

query:
After the group confirmed there would be a post-hike pub visit, one member's agreement contained a condition that revealed their real position on the trip. What did that condition signal about their actual attitude, and how would you have known from the way they phrased it?

Options:
A. Dev
B. Jonah
C. Marcus
D. Priya
context:
[1] (about=GROUP, said_by=Jonah, group-interaction, t4 @2025-10-19T19:15:00) Jonah asks about pub near bunkhouse in Hope for post-hike priorities.
[2] (about=Marcus, core, t6 @2025-10-26T18:01:00) Found a pub (Cheshire Cheese, 4.1 on Google) within 400 metres of the bunkhouse for post-hike.
[3] (about=Marcus, core, t2 @2025-10-12T17:46:00) A coat does not count as hiking gear; will book the bunkhouse Monday morning.
[4] (about=Priya, core, t10 @2025-11-09T19:31:00) Will not do another hike like Kinder Scout; prefers city trips with good design and identifiable food.
[5] (about=Priya, said_by=Jonah, profile, t2 @2025-10-12T17:46:00) Priya said she'd try a proper walk again, but Jonah notes she is reluctant about the November hike.
[6] (about=Priya, core, t2 @2025-10-12T17:46:00) Hesitant about November Peak District due to mud; considers 14km in mud a survival exercise, not a walk.
[7] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t10 @2025-11-09T19:31:00) Hike was not good; ankles hurt, mud, view only nice for four minutes before cloud came in.
[8] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t4 @2025-10-19T19:15:00) Priya agrees to pub as long as no hill on Sunday morning.
[9] (about=Simone, episodic, t10 @2025-11-09T19:48:00) December 19th. I fly January 6th. So there's time to do something properly before I go. I'd like that, if everyone's up for it. Something quiet. Not a party, just us.
agent_answer:
D. Priya

Priya agreed to the post-hike pub visit only **“as long as no hill on Sunday morning.”** That conditional phrasing signals that her real attitude toward the trip was reluctant, not enthusiastic: she needed the plan to avoid any further hill or tough hiking. It fits her broader stance — she found the 14km November hike in mud a “survival exercise, not a walk,” and prefers city trips. The words “as long as” reveal that her agreement was conditional, so her genuine position was hesitant about the trip itself.
